column1: Static code review - evidence-based findings from repository inspection. Scope: backend APIs/controllers/services, frontend controls and data flow. Updated October 2026 to include 4 interview-driven implementations.

column4: Expected Behavior
column7: Observed Defect / Implementation Note
column8: Recommended Fix / Action Taken

column4: Only an authenticated, authorized user can delete a complaint through a POST request protected against cross-site request forgery.
column7: Deletes a complaint when a GET id is supplied; starts a session but never checks user or role. A crafted link can trigger deletion for a logged-in user.
column8: Require POST, enforce Administrator/Lupon Clerk authorization, add CSRF validation, validate the ID, return a JSON result, and retain an audit record before deletion.

column4: Archive changes must be limited to authorized users and use an explicit protected mutation request.
column7: Accepts an id from GET or POST, performs no role check, and archives any valid complaint. The session is not used to authorize the action.
column8: Accept only POST, require the same role gate used by other complaint mutations, add CSRF protection, and reject missing or invalid IDs with 422.

column4: Case archival must authenticate the actor, validate the request method and case ID, and report failure accurately.
column7: Reads $_POST['case_id'] directly without a method check, session initialization, authorization, or input validation. The controller audit may reference an unset session user.
column8: Start the session, require POST and an authorized role, validate case_id with FILTER_VALIDATE_INT, return meaningful HTTP/JSON responses, and apply CSRF protection.

column4: A save response must reflect the result of a validated, authorized controller operation.
column7: Has no session or role check and always returns success after calling a non-existent SettlementController::create() method. This produces a fatal error or a false success contract depending on runtime handling.
column8: Retire or replace this route with SettlementController::save(), require authentication/RBAC/CSRF, validate input, and propagate the controller result and status code.

column4: Only authorized users can create an arbitration award and API output must reflect persistence success.
column7: No session or role check; always emits a success JSON payload even if ArbitrationController::create() returns false or throws.
column8: Require POST, RBAC and CSRF; validate request data; inspect the controller result and return 4xx/5xx failure payloads instead of unconditional success.

column4: Sensitive complaint, party, attachment, and case data must require an authenticated authorized session.
column7: Returns ComplaintController::show() without starting or checking a session. The controller includes parties, attachments, documents and workflow data.
column8: Require authenticated role-based access before loading the complaint and enforce record-level authorization if access is scoped by case/team.

column4: Case details should validate IDs and require an authorized reader.
column7: No session/RBAC check; directly reads $_GET['id'] and returns the case controller result. An unset id also generates a PHP notice.
column8: Start the session, validate id, return 422 for invalid input, and require an authorized role before querying the case.

column4: Dashboard data should be restricted to signed-in roles and fail safely.
column7: No session or role check before ReportController::dashboard() is called, exposing aggregate operational data to unauthenticated requests.
column8: Apply the dashboard role gate before controller construction and use a consistent JSON error response for unauthenticated/unauthorized callers.

column4: AI requests must require authentication, POST-only access, input length validation, and rate limits before sending data to an external provider.
column7: Both routes lack session/RBAC, method checks, request validation, and rate limiting. Any caller can trigger provider requests, and narrative input may include sensitive complaint details.
column8: Route through the hardened refine-narrative pattern: authenticate/authorize, validate bounded payloads, rate limit, document consent/privacy handling, and return controlled errors.

column4: Missing optional narrative fields should be handled without PHP notices and untrusted text should be bounded before prompt construction.
column7: Interpolates $data['who'], ['what'], ['when'], ['where'], ['why'], and ['how'] directly. Missing fields generate notices and unbounded input is sent to the AI service.
column8: Use null-coalescing defaults, validate per-field types and lengths, and use the documented refineNarrative-style prompt boundaries.

column4: Raw base64 uploads should be decoded, size-limited, and rejected before large allocations or provider requests.
column7: For string/base64 inputs, transcribeAudio() and ocrImage() accept the string without decoding or enforcing the documented 25 MB/15 MB limits. A large JSON body can consume application and provider resources.
column8: Validate allowed MIME types, estimate/decode base64 safely, enforce byte limits before request construction, and configure PHP request-size limits.

column4: Internal failure details should not be returned to clients, and scheduling constraints should be safe under concurrent requests.
column7: Exception handlers append $exception->getMessage() to the user response, leaking database or implementation details. Conflict checking occurs before persistence, so concurrent requests can both pass unless the model/database enforces the same constraint transactionally.
column8: Log detailed exceptions server-side and return a generic message with an error ID. Enforce final conflict/capacity validation inside the write transaction and add supporting uniqueness/locking where appropriate.

column4: Hearing schedules should not be created in the past unless an authorized exception is explicitly recorded.
column7: The source explicitly states that the future date restriction is bypassed for testing/development, leaving production behavior dependent on other checks.
column8: Restore server-side future-date validation with a narrowly scoped authorized override that records actor, reason, and audit history.

column4: Availability data should use the same role gate as the scheduling interface.
column7: Endpoint requires only user_id, unlike create/update/cancel which require Administrator or Lupon Clerk. This may disclose officer, venue, or schedule availability to roles that cannot schedule.
column8: Confirm the intended policy. If availability is operationally sensitive, require roles 1/2 or return a reduced availability response for other roles.

column3: Drafts, minor guardians, categories, and jurisdiction screening
column4: Drafts may remain incomplete; submitted complaints must validate category, narrative, parties, guardian requirements, map/location, jurisdiction screen, and duplicate acknowledgement.
column7: Reviewed implementation performs model-side validation for non-drafts and preserves draft behavior. Duplicate acknowledgement and jurisdiction screen are also checked on the server.
column8: Keep validation centralized in Complaint and add automated API coverage for the permitted draft and blocked submission paths.

column4: Uploads must validate files before moving them, use controlled storage paths, and remove partial files on failure.
column7: Reviewed ComplaintController attachment workflow validates uploaded files and cleans up a target file on database failure; download endpoint constrains resolved paths to approved upload directories.
column8: Add malware scanning and content-disposition hardening only if deployment policy requires it.

column3: Scheduling controls and async API responses
column4: Mutating hearing controls should accept only authorized POST requests and return a consistent success/failure response.
column7: Reviewed endpoints enforce POST and roles 1/2, validate hearing IDs where applicable, and return JSON status payloads consumed by the scheduling UI.
column8: Add end-to-end browser tests for disabled buttons, conflict messages, and retry behavior after a network error.

column4: User-derived text must be escaped before insertion into HTML; actions should not interpolate untrusted values into executable attributes.
column7: The reviewed primary screens frequently use innerHTML. Many visible fields are escaped, but the large codebase needs a focused taint review for every interpolated attribute/URL and inline onclick handler before declaring it XSS-safe.
column8: Standardize a DOM rendering helper, continue using escapeHtml for text, validate URL schemes/IDs separately, and add automated XSS payload tests for complaint, resident, document, and notification data.

column4: State-changing requests should verify a CSRF token or equivalent same-site anti-forgery mechanism.
column7: No shared CSRF middleware or token verification was found during the endpoint review; several mutations rely only on cookies/session state.
column8: Add a centralized CSRF token issue/validation middleware, include the token in all forms and fetch requests, and test rejection of missing/invalid tokens.

column4: Backend PHP files and frontend JavaScript files should parse before release.
column7: php -l passed on all 11 modified/created PHP files in the October 2026 implementation sprint (zero syntax errors). Logic unit tests verified state-transition correctness.
column8: Run PHP lint over every PHP file and node --check over every JavaScript file in CI, fail the build on any error, and retain the log as a release artifact.

column1: Mediation Stage: CaseStage.php / Hearing.php / MediationDeadlineService.php / stage-workspace.js
column3: Mediation 2-session ceiling and Pangkat auto-unlock (RA 7160 Sec. 410)
column4: Barangay Tumana policy limits mediation before the Punong Barangay to a maximum of 2 sessions. After the 2nd session fails, Pangkat Conciliation must unlock automatically without manual intervention.
column7: Previous implementation allowed up to 3 mediation sessions. The 3rd session booking guard, UI progress counters (3 of 3), banners, and session type labels all referenced an incorrect ceiling of 3.
column8: Changed max from 3 to 2 in CaseStage.php (completedMediationCount threshold, canBookNextMediation gate, referToPangkat guard), Hearing.php (activeMediationCount guard), MediationDeadlineService.php (advisory threshold), and stage-workspace.js (all UI labels, banners, progress counters, session type, error handler). php -l passed. No DB migration required.

column1: Case Details: backend/api/cases/reopen.php / CFA.php / complaint-details.php / complaints.js
column3: Reopen Settled cases for CFA issuance — non-compliance (RA 7160 Sec. 417)
column4: When a respondent fails to comply with Amicable Settlement terms, a Certificate to File Action must be issuable on a previously Settled case without corrupting existing settlement records.
column7: CFA.php blocked Settled cases unconditionally. No UI mechanism existed to reopen a Settled case for non-compliance CFA issuance. Settlement compliance_status was not updated on breach.
column8: Created backend/api/cases/reopen.php (POST, RBAC-gated) which marks settlements.compliance_status = Violated and logs case_history. Added isReopenWorkflow bypass in CFA.php. Added Reopen for CFA button (hidden unless Settled) and confirmation modal to complaint-details.php. JS functions (openReopenCfaModal, submitReopenForCfa) appended to complaints.js. php -l passed. No DB migration required (Violated already in ENUM).

column1: Reports: Report.php / ReportService.php / ReportController.php / export.php / report-list.php / reports.js
column3: Exportable Excel Case Register — 1-row-per-case with summons SLA (21 columns)
column4: Staff require a 1-row-per-case Excel-compatible spreadsheet with parties, summons delivery dates, timeliness SLA (On Time / Delayed / Not Served), hearing counts, settlement, and CFA outcome for DILG submission.
column7: Existing export produced a summary CSV (totals and categories only). No row-per-case register existed. Summons delivery timeliness was not computed or exported anywhere.
column8: Added getCaseRegister() to Report.php (joins summon_deliveries, hearings, settlements, cfa_records; computes SLA). Added createCaseRegisterExcel() to ReportService.php (UTF-8 BOM CSV, 21-column header). Added exportCaseRegister() to ReportController.php. export.php routed by format=register_excel. report-list.php gained date-range pickers and Export button. reports.js wired exportCaseRegister(). php -l passed. No DB migration required.

column3: DILG / LTIA 1-click printable Monthly / Quarterly Summary Report
column4: Staff require a printer-ready DILG/LTIA summary report (KPI summary, case status, categories, summons SLA, full case list, signature block) generatable in 1 click, without manual formatting.
column7: No printable report view existed. Staff manually compiled DILG submission data from the on-screen report table.
column8: Created backend/api/reports/print.php — self-contained HTML with @media print CSS, KPI grid, status/category tables, summons SLA boxes, full case list table, and signature block. Supports Monthly, Quarterly, Annual, and DILG types. Print DILG / LTIA Report button added to report-list.php. printDilgReport() added to reports.js (opens print.php in new tab). php -l passed.
